                                                                Abstract
          In the classical multi-armed bandit problem, d arms are available to the decision maker who
     pulls them sequentially in order to maximize his cumulative reward. Guarantees
                                                                                √         can be obtained
     on a relative quantity called regret, which scales linearly with d (or with d in the minimax sense).
     We here consider the sparse case of this classical problem in the sense that only a small number
     of arms, namely s < d, have a positive expected reward. We are able to leverage this additional
     assumption to provide an algorithm whose regret scales with s instead of d. Moreover, we prove that
     this algorithm is optimal by providing a matching lower bound – at least for a wide and pertinent
     range of parameters that we determine – and by evaluating its performance on simulated data.
     Keywords: stochastic multi-armed bandit problem, regret, sparsity, UCB

sumed to be i.i.d and of expectation µi . This problem is well understood, and there exist algorithms
